defects: The '7 VLM axis means' bar charts (Section 2 & 3) use indistinct row labels against dark backgrounds, forcing squinting to differentiate 'MEMORY' from 'TYPOGRAPHY'.
Excessive, unmodulated vertical whitespace (rhythm of ~100px) between major text blocks creates a disjointed scroll, breaking visual continuity in sections 3, 4, and 5.
The '7 gates' data table in Section 2 suffers from low contrast in its muted cells, and the 8 distinct status colors create visual noise rather than clear signal.
Typography scale lacks a clear middle tier; body copy sits uncomfortably close in size to subheads and monospace data rows, flattening the visual hierarchy.
The 'Unown' screenshot simulation in Section 4 acts as a heavy, disconnected visual block that clashes with the dark UI aesthetic of the surrounding page.
improvements: Tighten vertical spacing rhythm to a consistent 48px grid to create a calm, focused scroll experience.

critiques.label: Every great performance earns an encore.
defects: Body copy line height in the description paragraph is set too loose, creating a disjointed visual rhythm compared to the tight, professional headline spacing.
The color of the values in the bottom metric table (e.g., 6.50, 7.25) uses a muted maroon hue on a dark background, creating low contrast that violates accessibility standards for data legibility.
The two primary CTA buttons (gold and dark blue) are of identical weight and visual mass, lacking a clear primary/secondary distinction that would guide user intent effectively.
The typography in the bottom chart labels is extremely small and dense, functioning more like terminal metadata than a readable, well-scaled interface element for a desktop display.
There is an excessive amount of empty whitespace in the margins on the left and right, causing the content to feel vertically center-aligned but spatially lost in a desktop viewport band.
improvements: Reduce the line-height of the main description paragraph to tighten the reading flow.
Increase the contrast of the values in the metric table by using a brighter gold or white color.
Make the gold 'See the loop' button slightly larger or more prominent to establish clear visual hierarchy.

critiques.label: The receipt before the fix
defects: The red 'FAIL' status color and numbers have low contrast against the dark blue card background, failing WCAG AA for legibility.
The repetition of '20261029_e-root.json' under every single metric in the summary grid is visual noise that breaks the calm density.
The 'FAIL' pill badge next to the large 6.40 score feels disproportionately small and visually disconnected from the primary data point.
The gold/yellow color used for 'PASS' status and 'THE BASELINE' label lacks distinctiveness, creating a muddy semantic state against the warm brand palette.
The '11 gates' section header feels cramped and lacks vertical breathing room before the grid of metrics begins.
improvements: Increase contrast for red status text and add a subtle background tint to the pill badges.
Remove redundant file path labels from individual metrics; centralize metadata in the card header.
Expand the 'FAIL' badge size to match the visual weight of the 6.40 score.

critiques.label: A measured critique loop, receipted
defects: The gold accent on the '1. build' active state is severely washed out, destroying contrast ratios and losing the 'warm ink' brand promise
The '1/6' metadata label lacks sufficient vertical whitespace from the step title, creating a cramped, accidental collision
The footer technical paragraph has no visual demarcation (like a subtle top border or reduced opacity), making it read as noise rather than metadata
The gap between the sub-header paragraph and the horizontal step-pill row is disproportionately large compared to the tight card interior spacing
Using gold on the 'THE LOOP' eyebrow text and buttons against the dark background creates a glaring, high-glare effect that competes with the H1
improvements: Deepen gold to amber, raising button/eyebrow contrast ratios for legibility
Add a 1px top border to the metadata paragraph for clear separation
Shrink the vertical gutter between the paragraph and the step-pill row

critiques.label: Before and after, receipted
defects: Eyebrow 'THE ITERATIONS' is disproportionately large; the uppercase treatment fights the h1 instead of yielding to it, blurring the hierarchy between section and sub-section.
The interaction hint (keyboard shortcut) is orphaned in the negative space, failing to visually tether to the interactive artifact it explains, breaking the logical reading flow.
Bottom caption text (before/after receipts) lacks sufficient color contrast against the dark-navy background, failing WCAG legibility standards for secondary text.
Vertical rhythm is inconsistent: the generous 40px+ gap between the paragraph and the screenshot is arbitrary, while the 'receipted' caption at the very bottom feels cramped and disconnected.
The gold used for the eyebrow and the UI buttons introduces a competing 'warm' accent that undermines the requested 'warm paper/ink' aesthetic, creating visual noise against the cool dark-navy.
improvements: Reduce eyebrow font size to 12px and add 200ms of letter-spacing to establish superior restraint.
Attach interaction hints directly to the artifact border with a subtle, low-opacity gold pill.
Increase bottom caption font size to 14px and shift color to 'warm-gray' for WCAG compliance.

critiques.label: Two tools, built this round
defects: The 'HEADLINE' box in the left card is too prominent; its bold text and large type weight creates a jarring visual interruption that competes with the card title.
Contrast is low on 'receipt: design-critic' and 'Provenance' text; the dark blue on dark blue background is illegible and fails WCAG AA on small text.
The bar graph in the right card has a misaligned '1.50' label floating in space with no clear relation to the bar's length or axis, making it hard to read.
The gold 'THE TOOLS' eyebrow label and section header are close in color, reducing visual separation; the eyebrow should be bolder or more distinct.
The cards have too much vertical padding, creating dead space between the body text and the receipt line; the content feels vertically stretched.
improvements: Reduce the 'HEADLINE' box impact; use a border only, not a filled background, and smaller font weight.
Increase contrast on 'receipt' and 'Provenance' lines to light gray (minimum #888) for WCAG AA compliance.
Tighten the vertical spacing inside cards; reduce padding to create a denser, more balanced composition.

critiques.label: Every failure became a benchmark
defects: The 'CLOSED' status badges lack visual distinction; their border-only style competes with the F10/F11 identifiers rather than signaling state.
Fix-reference links (e.g., 'docs/website-excellence-session.md') use a generic gold underline that breaks the hand-drawn brand language and feels like a hyperlink, not a receipt.
Excessive vertical whitespace between the two ledger cards and the closing paragraph creates a disjointed rhythm, undermining the 'calm density' goal.
The sub-headline text ('The round's POs and PIs...') has low contrast against the dark background, failing WCAG AA for small text sizes.
The F10 and F11 cards are identical in structure but lack a subtle visual anchor (like a left-border or icon) to differentiate the failure ID from the description text.
improvements: Increase sub-headline contrast to at least 4.5:1 against the background for accessibility compliance.
Reduce vertical spacing between cards and text to establish a tighter, more rhythmic flow.
Restyle fix-reference links with hand-drawn glyphs or a distinct underline to match the brand.

critiques.label: The question the round set out to answer
defects: Excessive vertical whitespace between the top paragraph and 'THE FINALE' disrupts the visual flow and makes the layout feel fragmented rather than cohesive.
The large empty gap between the CTA buttons and the footer metadata creates an unbalanced bottom section that feels disconnected from the primary content cluster above.
The code-like metadata text at the bottom center is too low-contrast and small, making it difficult to read against the dark background without straining.
The blockquote's gold left border is thin and visually underweight compared to the boldness of the main heading, causing it to lack sufficient presence.
The two CTA buttons, while distinct, have slightly uneven visual weight due to the primary button's bright gold fill competing aggressively with the dark ghost button.
improvements: Reduce the vertical gap between the top paragraph and the section header to tighten the flow.
Increase the bottom footer text size and opacity to improve legibility and anchor the layout.
Bold the gold blockquote border to match the visual weight of the header and improve hierarchy.

defects: The 'Before/After' comparison mockup uses low-contrast pastel colors that undermine the WCAG legibility claim on the warm paper background
The 'Axis-by-axis data' table has poor visual rhythm; baseline, current, and delta columns lack strong typographic distinction
Hero section secondary text is slightly cramped against the action buttons, breaking the calm density elsewhere on the page
The 'VLM axis means' and 'Hermes' bar charts are identical in visual weight, causing the user's eye to bounce rather than flow hierarchically
Monospace terminal snippets lack sufficient padding and line-height to match the precision of the surrounding serif typography
improvements: Increase baseline table column padding and add a muted vertical rule to improve data scanability
Boost hero subtext line-height by 10% to restore the breathing room lost in that section
Introduce a subtle background hue shift to the 'After' mockup to anchor it visually against the paper

defects: The 'hand-drawn' brand glyphs are reduced to illegible, cramped data bars in the 'Baseline' section, destroying the visual metaphor.
Spacing rhythm is completely broken: the '6.40' score is crammed tightly against the 2x2 stats grid with inconsistent vertical padding.
Typography scale is chaotic: the monospace font is used for everything (headers, data, code, captions), causing a loss of typographic hierarchy.
Contrast is poor: the orange/gold text on the mid-tone dark blue background falls below WCAG AA, particularly on the 'FAIL' labels.
Visual alignment is inconsistent: the 'gates' table mixes left-aligned text with right-aligned numbers without a clear column rule.
improvements: Increase vertical breathing room between section headers and their data grids to restore calm density.

critiques.label: Every great performance earns an encore.
defects: Inconsistent CTA hierarchy: primary 'See the loop' and secondary 'Read the receipts' share identical visual weight and vertical padding, failing to establish clear action priority.
Orphaned microcopy at bottom ('Baseline axis means...') floats in unstructured whitespace, disconnected from the header and main content, breaking the visual rhythm.
The 'encore' headline word is colored gold but lacks sufficient contrast against the dark navy background, failing WCAG AA legibility standards.
Vertical spacing between the hero block, paragraph text, and CTA buttons is uneven, creating a disjointed, floating feel rather than a cohesive column.
The small top label 'ENCORE' is too small and low-contrast to function effectively as a section identifier in mobile viewport.
improvements: Brighten the 'encore' gold text or add a subtle text-shadow for better legibility.

critiques.label: The receipt before the fix
defects: Red-on-dark contrast (6.40, FAIL) is a WCAG catastrophe; fail-state text is effectively unreadable against the navy background.
The 2x2 data grid has no visual gridlines, causing left and right columns to blur into a chaotic, unstructured block.
The monospaced filenames under every metric are truncated and redundant, adding immense visual noise without providing context.
The vertical rhythm is broken by the cramped 11 gates section, where row padding is inconsistent with the spacing of the main metrics above.
The PASS/FAIL indicators clash with their respective text colors; the red FAIL text on a reddish-tinted dark background has poor legibility.
improvements: Increase red hex brightness to 3.5:1+ for WCAG AA compliance on all fail-states.
Add 1px vertical borders to the metrics grid to enforce column alignment.
Remove redundant filenames; consolidate metadata into a single collapsible footer.

critiques.label: A measured critique loop, receipted
defects: Visual weight of the active '1. build' state is too subtle; the gold border is lost against the dark card background and competes with the static step numbers.
Inconsistent spacing rhythm: the vertical gap between the step-pill grid and the large detail card is too tight compared to the generous whitespace above the H1.
The bottom utility text uses a low-contrast slate-grey that likely fails WCAG AA against the navy background.
The '1/6' progress indicator in the card header is visually weak and lacks clear typographic hierarchy compared to the bold 'build' title.
The monospace code snippet lacks distinct background shading or syntax highlighting, blending poorly with the surrounding description text.
improvements: Increase active pill border thickness and add a subtle gold glow to establish clear focus state.
Increase vertical margin below the step-pill grid to match the consistent rhythmic 8pt spacing scale.
Brighten the bottom body text to off-white to ensure WCAG-compliant contrast on the dark background.

critiques.label: Before and after, receipted
defects: The 'Hierachy' (typo of Hierarchy) data table at the very bottom completely lacks zebra-stripes or row dividers, making the numbers 6.50, 6.50, and 0.00 visually merge into an unreadable block against the dark background.

The caption text beneath the interactive drag-comparison modal is crammed into a single, poorly-aligned line ('before - receipt: baseline after - receipt: baseline — in flight'), failing basic WCAG line-length and whitespace principles.

The 'Axis-by-axis delta' section header immediately below the screenshot introduces a completely new data-dense module but is completely broken off at the mobile viewport boundary, leaving the user with a jarring cliff-edge with no visual cue of continuation.

The typographic hierarchy between the 'BEFORE / AFTER' labels and the '6.40' values inside the modal is completely lost; both sit in the same muted, low-contrast pill style, failing to establish which element is the state and which is the metric.

There is a massive, unexplained visual void between the primary body paragraph and the sub-instruction text ('Drag to reveal the after state...'), breaking the established 8pt spacing rhythm and diluting the section's narrative flow.
improvements: Fix 'Hierachy' typo and add distinct row backgrounds or dividers to the bottom data table.
Format the 'receipt: baseline' captions into clean, stacked two-line lists using proper whitespace.
Ensure the 'Axis-by-axis delta' module has enough bottom padding to not crop on scroll.

critiques.label: Two tools, built this round
defects: The mobile type scale is broken: the 'HEADLINE' overline inside the receipt box is rendered at roughly the same visual weight as the body copy above it, creating no hierarchy.
Contrast failure: the muted grey body text ('The design critic...') and the secondary link ('receipt:...') appear to hover around 4:1 on the dark navy background, failing WCAG AA for non-large text.
The 'HEADLINE' label is visually disconnected from the golden verdict text below it due to inconsistent vertical tracking, making the callout look like two separate, unrelated UI elements.

The right edge of the '6.40 baseline, verdict FAIL...' callout box sits flush against the right margin of its parent container, creating a cramped, unpolished feeling that breaks the section's outer padding rhythm.
The spacing rhythm is inconsistent: there is a large vertical gap between the H2 and the paragraph, but a tighter gap between the paragraph and the first card, disrupting the section's visual flow.
improvements: Increase 'HEADLINE' size to 14px and add letter-spacing to separate it from the 16px body.
Boost secondary text contrast to at least #9CA3AF to pass WCAG AA.
Add 24px internal padding to the golden verdict callout box.
Unify vertical spacing to a strict 8px grid throughout the section.
Increase top padding on the 'design_critic.mjs' card for visual balance.

critiques.label: Every failure became a benchmark
defects: Low contrast on 'F10' and 'F11' tag labels: light blue text on the mid-blue card background fails WCAG AA legibility standards.
Cognitive density in F10 card: the root cause, fix, and CPO are lumped into a single text block without hierarchy or visual separation.
Typography inconsistency: 'CLOSED' status badge uses a monospaced font while body copy is a sans-serif, breaking the type rhythm.
Awkward line-wrapping in the H1 'Every failure became a benchmark' where 'a benchmark' feels disconnected from the leading phrase.
improvements: Brighten the F-number tag labels to gold or off-white to meet strict contrast requirements.

critiques.label: The question the round set out to answer
defects: The 22px '6.40' gold metric lacks WCAG contrast against the #1B2A4B card background (ratio ~2.8:1 vs 4.5:1 needed for large text).
Italicized quote with gold left border creates visual noise; the border extends past the text block's vertical rhythm, breaking the 8px spacing scale.
'Back to the gallery' CTA (solid gold) has stronger visual weight than 'Read the session log' (ghost), inverting intent priority for a finale section.
Type scale inconsistency: 'THE FINALE' eyebrow (11px, tracking +2px) sits below the 32px H2 with no consistent modular ratio between eyebrow/H2/lede/quote/card-body.
Card padding (24px) creates 40px gap to the H2 above, then 32px gap to CTA row — inconsistent vertical rhythm that disrupts section pacing.
improvements: Raise '6.40' gold to #FFD700 and card bg to #0F172A for WCAG 4.5:1 contrast
Align gold quote border to text cap-height, remove 12px overhang at bottom edge
Establish 8pt modular scale: eyebrow 11/13, H2 32/40, lede 16/24, body 14/20, metric 28/34
Invert CTA visual weight: make 'Read the session log' solid gold, 'Back' ghost
